questions.answer:
Inclusivity means recognizing, accommodating and meeting the learning needs of all your
learners. It means acknowledging that your learners have a range of individual learning needs and are
members of diverse communities. Inclusivity means making sure everyone feels welcome, valued, and
respected, no matter who they are or where they come from.
By fostering and promoting an inclusive learning culture, training and/or assessment organization can:
Prepare its learners to work more effectively and flexibly in diverse workplaces and communities
Page 5
Provide more learners and clients with better quality services in an increasingly competitive market
Ensure it meets its obligations arising out of legislation and standard
questions.question: What is inclusivity? Why practice inclusivity?
What principles should be integrated into work practices to foster an inclusive learning culture?

Women where under represented

People with disability

questions.answer:
Support persons assist learners to overcome barriers and participate fully in training and
assessment.
Examples and Roles:
Teacher Aides / Learning Support Officers: 1. Help learners with disabilities during training or
assessments. 2. Provide one-on-one guidance or assist with equipment.
Interpreters / Translators: 1. Assist learners with limited English proficiency or hearing impairment. 2.
Translate instructions, questions, or responses.
Counsellors / Student Advisors: 1. Provide emotional, social, or career support. 2. Help learners manage
stress or personal issues affecting learning.
Mentors / Peer Support: 1. Guide learners through tasks or practical activities. 2. Encourage
participation and build confidence.
Family Members / Carers (where appropriate): 1. Assist with mobility, communication, or personal care
needs during training.

questions.answer:
Maintenance is performing the routine actions which keep the device in working order, to keep
in good condition, to preserve and protect the device.
questions.question: What is maintenance?

questions.answer:
Meaning: Preventive - Planned maintenance done before a fault occurs; Corrective -
Maintenance done after a fault or breakdown occurs
Page 6
Purpose: Preventive - To prevent breakdown and extend equipment life; Corrective - To repair the fault
and restore the equipment to working condition
Timing: Preventive - Scheduled / regular (daily, weekly, monthly); Corrective - Unscheduled, when a
failure happens
Examples: Preventive - Cleaning, oiling, adjusting, routine replacement of parts; Corrective - Fixing a
broken part, replacing a part after breakdown
Cost / downtime: Preventive - Lower cost, less downtime; Corrective - Higher cost, more downtime
